answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on reputation or claim shared rewards. The protocol caps each account’s influence by that stake and slashes it when repeated, independently verified fraud is proven, so splitting funds across sybils does not create extra weight. A pigment or quill can label a ridge in the audit trail, but neither grants trust: the attacker must tie up real capital and risk losing it for every identity.
